No, first confirm warehouse receipt and inspection.
Only if the customer closes the browser.
92.explanation: No. RTO initiated indicates a return process, not warehouse receipt or sellable condition. Track the parcel, receive it and inspect it before restocking under policy. Money and refund decisions remain separate from the movement status.
nodeDetails: An NDR reason should be checked against current courier evidence.
The store records a supported next action and required information.
An accepted action can still be pending or fail.
Receipt and inspection provide evidence for stock handling.

choices: Delivered and bank-settled, because the statuses must match.
Mark unpaid and request a second customer charge.
Delivered and collected, with remittance pending reconciliation.
93.explanation: Delivered, collection confirmed, remittance pending or under reconciliation. Check the provider remittance record, applicable deductions and bank evidence separately. Do not charge again, invent a settlement date, or mark the cash as bank-received solely from tracking.
nodeDetails: Carrier movement and customer payment collection are different evidence streams.
Record quantities and condition before deciding sellable inventory.
An approved refund still needs a recorded successful money movement.
Match provider statements and bank evidence to the order ledger.

choices: Any amount, then fix it in the browser.
50000 minor units from the server quote.
1 minor unit because it came from hosted checkout.
94.explanation: Use the authenticated cart and trusted prices to compute 50000 INR minor units, then link the provider order to that internal attempt. Reject or ignore the untrusted total under the API contract. Hosted checkout does not replace server pricing.
nodeDetails: Verify identity and cart ownership before reading private items.
Use integer minor units and the agreed quote, tax and shipping policy.
Persist a stable logical operation and its requested amount before the external call.
Razorpay Orders are created server-side; retain the returned reference.
Expose the appropriate key identifier and order reference, never the server key secret.

choices: Paid immediately because the browser redirected.
Failed immediately, then ask the customer to pay again.
Pending verification, then reconcile the existing attempt.
95.explanation: Keep a clearly named pending-verification state, show reassuring but accurate customer text, and reconcile the existing attempt. Do not ship, claim verified payment, or create another charge solely because the webhook is delayed.
nodeDetails: The browser supplies a clue that must be tied to a stored operation.
Checkout proof and webhook signatures use different inputs and secrets.
Match the stored provider order, amount, currency and applicable payment state.
A unique provider-event record and guarded business transition prevent duplicate effects.
Use provider evidence to resolve missed, delayed or contradictory notifications.

choices: Keep paid and settlement-pending states separate.
Mark payment failed because the bank has not received it.
Create another charge to make settlement happen.
96.explanation: No. Preserve the verified captured payment and track settlement separately. Investigate delayed settlement through provider and bank records. A refund also needs its own state and reconciliation; changing the payment history to failed would destroy useful evidence.
nodeDetails: Authorization is not assumed to be capture. Inspect the actual method and account configuration.
Razorpay supports capture settings; fulfill only under the agreed verified-payment policy.
Track refund amount, reason, permissions, operation key and provider reference.
Settlement groups eligible monetary activity and adjustments.
Confirm actual bank receipt independently from the shopper payment outcome.

choices: Put account passwords in receipt templates to avoid reset flows.
Separate service-message purpose from marketing preference.
Send every receipt as a newsletter campaign.
97.explanation: Keep password recovery and order notifications tied to their specific service purpose, and maintain a distinct marketing preference. Use the auth system for recovery-token lifecycle and a verified sender domain. Do not assume one opt-in flag covers every jurisdiction or channel.
nodeDetails: The event defines why this message exists.
Resolve the intended recipient from trusted account/order records.
Render only required fields and protect recovery tokens.
Use documented domain verification and email authentication settings.
Channel and purpose determine the approved communication policy.

choices: Generate a fresh idempotency key and resend automatically.
Assume the queue permanently prevents all duplicate effects.
Use a durable completed intent plus provider evidence.
98.explanation: The application notification ledger must remember the completed business intent beyond the provider window. A durable unique key handles repeated events. For uncertain old sends, reconcile rather than blindly retrying with a new key. A provider key is useful but is not permanent business history.
nodeDetails: Repeated copies can describe the same business occurrence.
Uniqueness maps the occurrence, recipient, channel and template policy to one intent.
A worker may receive the job again after a crash.
Reuse the documented idempotency mechanism where supported.
Store provider ID, attempt evidence and outcome for later reconciliation.

choices: Record the bounce and follow address/suppression policy.
Mark the order unpaid because email bounced.
Keep resending forever because the send API returned success.
99.explanation: Update notification delivery evidence and apply the appropriate suppression or address-correction workflow. Keep payment and order status unchanged. A permanent failure does not become success by retrying the same invalid destination repeatedly.
nodeDetails: The provider reference links later callbacks to the saved intent.
Verify the actual provider request scheme before trusting callback fields.
Email and SMS states have different meanings; map them deliberately.
Respect suppression and communication policy before any retry or alternate channel.
Log safe IDs and error categories, not message bodies or full contact details.

choices: The provider should receive the application secret in its callback URL.
Loopback points to the caller’s own machine.
CORS blocks every server-to-server webhook.
100.explanation: Loopback refers to the machine making the request. The provider is not running on your laptop. Diagnose reachability and the provider’s callback restrictions; do not disable authentication or publish the whole course to solve a synthetic exercise.
nodeDetails: A domain and its subdomains identify names, not permissions.
DNS answers where to connect; caches and records can delay a change.
A valid certificate must cover the hostname and preserve connection trust.
The path, method and environment must resolve to the expected handler.
Reachable traffic still needs provider authentication and application validation.

choices: Allow all origins and skip ownership checks.
Move the session secret into a query string.
Preserve 403 and test with an owned order.
101.explanation: Nothing should relax the ownership check. CORS permission is not permission to read that order. Confirm the session, actor and requested resource, then preserve the rejection. Use a valid owned order to test a successful application request.
nodeDetails: Compare scheme, host and port; inspect OPTIONS when present.
Cookie attributes and fetch credentials affect which cookies travel.
The server verifies the credential rather than trusting a browser claim.
State changes require the appropriate anti-CSRF and resource-level access rules.
A browser-readable response may still be an intentional 403 error.

choices: Verify server identity and authorize that exact order.
Trust it because the customer logged in.
Hide the order button and leave the API unchanged.
102.explanation: Server-side resource authorization must reject it before returning data or causing an effect. A random-looking ID, CORS header or hidden button is not an access policy. Test the direct request with two customers and record the denied result.
nodeDetails: Treat supplied text, identifiers, filenames and URLs as untrusted.
Parameterized queries and safe rendering address different injection contexts.
Derive identity and check access to the specific order or file.
Bound bytes, rate, query cost and external-service spending.
Keep updates reviewable and revoke any exposed credential.

choices: Only the text Something went wrong with no reference.
Safe IDs, stage, duration and an uncertain outcome.
The full card payload and API secret.
103.explanation: Record the operation/correlation ID, safe internal and provider references, stage, duration, outcome and redacted error category. Do not log secrets or full payment/customer payloads. A missing response should be labeled uncertain until provider evidence resolves it.
nodeDetails: Start with what failed for the learner or customer.
Structured fields let events be filtered and joined.
Measurements reveal the scale and trend of the problem.
Trace spans identify the boundary consuming time or returning an error.
A useful alert names impact, responsibility and the next evidence to inspect.

choices: Double every worker and remove retry limits.
Delete all queued jobs and report the incident resolved.
Limit pressure and investigate the constrained dependency.
104.explanation: Reduce the pressure and inspect connection ownership, long transactions and slow queries before increasing workers. Preserve jobs and diagnose the dependency. Once repaired, replay a bounded sample with duplicate protection and compare queue age, errors and business records.
nodeDetails: Age of oldest work shows user delay better than count alone.
Classify transient dependency failure, poison payload and expired credential.
Inspect active connections, wait states and transaction duration.
Fix the actual issue instead of hiding it with more retries.
Reuse stable operation IDs and verify that replay produces no duplicate booking or charge.

choices: Reconcile the existing provider operation before any new charge.
Charge again because the restored row is unpaid.
Delete the provider evidence so it matches the restored database.
105.explanation: Reconcile the trusted provider record to the intended order and rebuild or review the missing local attempt. Do not charge again based solely on the restored state. Preserve an audit record and verify amount, currency, ownership and stock decisions before resuming fulfillment.
nodeDetails: Agree tolerable loss and downtime, then measure the actual drill.
Cover database, files, configuration and recovery access.
Disable outbound payment, shipment and notification effects during the drill.
Compare payments, orders, reservations, shipping and refunds by stable references.
Reopen only after critical invariants and monitoring have evidence.

choices: Accept the profile role and skip the ownership check.
Reject B and preserve A’s cart.
Allow B because both customers are logged in.
106.explanation: No. A valid session establishes B’s identity, not access to A’s cart. Deny the operation without revealing private cart details or changing records. Then demonstrate the successful request with A and verify the saved cart after a reload.
nodeDetails: Use trusted session verification, not user-editable role data.
The catalog exposes approved product information and authoritative variant pricing.
Check the requested cart against the authenticated customer.
Persist the item and quantity under a stable cart reference.
Render the committed result or a useful failure; refresh checks durability.

choices: onHand 0, reserved 1, available-1.
onHand 1, reserved 0, available 1.
onHand 1, reserved 1, available 0.
107.explanation: Keep onHand 1 and reserved 1, so available 0. Payment confirms the allocation but does not consume physical stock a second time. Shipment later changes onHand and reserved together to 0. A duplicate capture must leave those counts unchanged.
nodeDetails: Freeze the agreed amount, currency and item information for this checkout.

Reconcile the existing attempt using verified provider evidence.
Keep purchased details even if the catalog later changes.
Record downstream shipping/notification work with the confirmed transition.

choices: Recover and match the existing shipment S-1.
Create a fresh booking immediately after every timeout.
Mark the order delivered because a shipment record exists.
108.explanation: Link and recover the existing S-1 after matching order and package evidence. Do not create a duplicate booking. Booking alone does not prove physical shipment. Continue tracking, return inspection and refund state changes with their own evidence and permissions.
nodeDetails: Keep internal order, provider shipment and tracking references distinct.

Normalize provider statuses while retaining original evidence and event timing.
